questions_for_integrator: Does s-bend progress return to about 0.148, which would confirm that the wheel_radius 0.035 m and wheel_track 0.16 m change cost progress on that track?
At what progress does the single line loss occur on each track? If it is the same progress on all three tracks, the loss is a fixed point such as the start or one bend.
Does max_error reach 0.06 m before or after the line loss, on the oval and slalom?

intent: Restore the iteration 0 baseline by reverting wheel_radius to 0.03 m and wheel_track to 0.12 m, with the iteration 0 sensing and mass 0.8 kg. The aim is to recover the s-bend progress lost in iteration 6 (0.135 against 0.1476) and the best score so far (about 52.3). Expected result: progress near 0.14 on the oval and 0.15 on the s-bend, line_loss_events about 1.0 per run, and max_error at or near the 0.06 m off-track limit.
learning: Iterations 0 to 6 show that sensing span, sensor size, forward offset, mass, wheel radius and wheel track each leave line loss at about 1.0 per run. Progress separates the high and low scores. If this run reproduces about 52 with line loss still at 1.0, the next step is per-track telemetry on where the loss occurs, and then a sensor_size 0.008 test on the same five-sensor layout.
rationale: Iteration 6 restored the iteration 0 sensing (five 12 mm sensors, x -0.02 to +0.02 m, y 0.05 m, mass 0.8 kg) and kept wheel_radius 0.035 m and wheel_track 0.16 m. It scored 51.63, close to the best of 52.28. Oval progress recovered to 0.1446 from 0.138, which supports the sensing as the driver of the earlier progress loss. S-bend progress stayed lower at 0.135 against 0.1476 in iteration 0, and it is the only track where the dynamics changed without a gain. Line_loss_events stayed at 1.0 on s-bend and slalom and 1.2 on oval, so the loss is still a fixed point and no geometry change has removed it. Steering oscillation stayed low at 0.09 to 0.13, so the robot is not jittering. Following the Integrator's decision rule (2), I revert wheel_radius to 0.03 m and wheel_track to 0.12 m, the iteration 0 values that gave the best s-bend progress, and keep the iteration 0 sensing and mass. I expect a score near 52.3 with line loss still at about 1.0 per run. This run is a confirmation of the iteration 0 baseline, and the telemetry requested will show where on the course the single loss occurs, which is the next thing to learn.
